exams.name: State Board Examination (podiatry subjects)
exams.notes: Subjects include anatomy, histology, physiology, chemistry, pharmacy, materia medica, therapeutics, bacteriology, pathology, surgery, dermatology, neurology, physical therapy, diagnosis and roentgenology, orthopedics, chiropody and chiropodial surgery. Minimum 75% general average; no subject below 60%.
exams.quote: Any person not exempt from examination under Section 73-27-5 ... and desiring a license to practice podiatry shall, upon application to the State Board of Medical Licensure ... be examined in the following subjects: anatomy, histology, physiology, chemistry, pharmacy, materia medica, therapeutics, bacteriology, pathology, surgery, dermatology, neurology, physical therapy, diagnosis and roentgenology, orthopedics, chiropody and chiropodial surgery

exams.name: National Board of Chiropody or Podiatry Licensure (optional affiliation)
exams.notes: The board may affiliate with the National Board of Chiropody or Podiatry Licensure in granting licenses, provided the written examination covers at least two-thirds of the subjects set forth in Section 73-27-9.
exams.jurisdiction: national (National Board of Chiropody or Podiatry Licensure)
exams.quote: The State Board of Medical Licensure may affiliate with the National Board of Chiropody or Podiatry Licensure in granting licenses to practice podiatry in Mississippi, provided the written examination covers at least two-thirds (2/3) of the subjects set forth in Section 73-27-9

interval_years.quote: the license of every person licensed to practice podiatry in the State of Mississippi shall be renewed annually

renewal_fee_usd.quote: submit it to the board in the manner prescribed by the board in the notice before June 30 with the renewal fee of an amount established by the board, but not to exceed Three Hundred Dollars ($300.00)

available.quote: Upon payment of a fee prescribed by the State Board of Medical Licensure, not to exceed Five Hundred Dollars ($500.00), a license without examination may be issued to podiatrists of other states maintaining equal statutory requirements for the practice of podiatry and extending the same reciprocal privileges to this state.

requirements.value: Reciprocal state must maintain equal statutory requirements and extend the same reciprocal privileges to Mississippi; fee not to exceed $500. Also subject to universal recognition provisions under Sections 73-50-1 and 73-50-2 for military-trained applicants, military spouses, and persons establishing Mississippi residence.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Habitual personal use of narcotic drugs or drugs with addiction-forming or addiction-sustaining liability.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Habitual personal use of narcotic drugs, or any other drug having addiction-forming or addiction-sustaining liability.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Habitual use of intoxicating liquors to an extent which affects professional competency.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Habitual use of intoxicating liquors, or any beverage, to an extent which affects professional competency.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Administering, dispensing or prescribing narcotic drugs or controlled substances outside legitimate professional practice.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Administering, dispensing or prescribing any narcotic drug, or any other drug having addiction-forming or addiction-sustaining liability otherwise than in the course of legitimate professional practice.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Conviction of violation of any federal or state law regulating possession, distribution or use of narcotic drugs or controlled substances.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Conviction of violation of any federal or state law regulating the possession, distribution or use of any narcotic drug or any drug considered a controlled substance under state or federal law.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Performing medical diagnosis or treatment outside the scope of podiatry.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Performing any medical diagnosis or treatment outside the scope of podiatry as defined in Section 73-27-1.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Conviction of a felony or misdemeanor involving moral turpitude.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Conviction of a felony or misdemeanor involving moral turpitude.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Obtaining or attempting to obtain a license by fraud or deception.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Obtaining or attempting to obtain a license by fraud or deception.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Unprofessional conduct including false names, assisting unlicensed persons, fraudulent claims, dishonest or unethical conduct, fraudulent fee collection, false documents, or failure to identify school of practice.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Unprofessional conduct, which includes, but is not limited to: Practicing medicine under a false or assumed name or impersonating another practitioner, living or dead.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Refusal, revocation, suspension or other restriction of a license by another state's licensing authority.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: The refusal of a licensing authority of another state to issue or renew a license, permit or certificate to practice podiatry in that state or the revocation, suspension or other restriction imposed on a license, permit or certificate issued by such licensing authority which prevents or restricts practice in that state.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violation of provisions relating to deceptive advertisement by health care practitioners (repealed effective 7/1/2025).
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Violation(s) of the provisions of Sections 41-121-1 through 41-121-9 relating to deceptive advertisement by health care practitioners. This paragraph shall stand repealed on July 1, 2025.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Being out of compliance with an order for support.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: the board shall be authorized to suspend the license of any licensee for being out of compliance with an order for support

definition_quote.value: The practice of podiatric medicine is that profession concerned with the prevention, examination, diagnosis and medical, surgical and adjuvant treatment of conditions of the human foot. For the purposes of this chapter, 'foot' means that part of the human anatomy which consists of the tarsal bones, metatarsal bones and phalanges.
